papers.what_it_is: A Quantum Computing Inc educational web lesson giving a high-level overview of quantum optics, non-linear optics, interference, the Hong-Ou-Mandel effect and the company's lithium niobate chip approach.

assertions.value: The page states that weakening the strength of a light source such as a laser or a light bulb does not make quantum effects apparent, even when a pulse holds on average a single photon or less.
quotes: just weakening the strength of a light source such as a laser or a light bulb does not make quantum effects apparent.
This is even the case if it is weakened so much that on average a pulse of light only contains a single particle (photon), or even less than one.
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement in a vendor's educational page; the page gives no proof and defers the mathematical explanation.
assertions.reader_inference: This is standard physics (a weak coherent state stays classical-like), stated here without derivation.

assertions.value: The page defines non-linear optics, in its use, as the case where photons are allowed to interact with each other through an underlying material, which lets the company turn ordinary light such as laser light into more interesting types of light.
quotes: Non-linear optics addresses cases where photons are allowed to interact with each other through an underlying material.
This allows us to turn more mundane types of light, such as those produced by a laser, into more interesting types of light.
assertions.certainty_reason: The page's own definition of the term it relies on, Non-linear optics section.

assertions.value: The page states that without interactions between photons the company can produce pulses with one particle on average but cannot produce a pulse known for sure to have exactly one, and that interaction through a non-linear medium overcomes this limit.
quotes: Without interactions between them, the particles will act independently, with no influence from the other ones
we can produce pulses where there is one particle on average , but not produce a pulse that we know for sure has exactly one.
If light particles are able to interact through a non-linear medium it is clear to see that this limitation can be overcome.
assertions.certainty_reason: A conceptual argument in a vendor's educational page, without derivation.
assertions.reader_inference: The page's claim that interaction in a medium is needed for a known exact photon number is a simplification; heralded single-photon sources are the usual route and also rely on non-linear processes.

assertions.value: The page states that resonance is the key concept in the company's non-linear crystals, that energy and momentum conservation let the company control what happens to the light, and that many of its devices use whispering gallery modes.
quotes: The key concept in our nonlinear crystals is resonance .
Physical processes have to conserve energy and momentum.
Many of our devices use whispering gallery modes similar to the resonances in sound
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own product.

assertions.value: The page states that how strongly the crystals make light interact depends on how strong the local electromagnetic fields can be made, and that confining light to a smaller space strengthens these fields and therefore the interactions.
quotes: How strongly these crystals make the light interact depends on how strong the local electromagnetic fields can be made, confining light to a smaller space strengthens these fields and therefore the interactions.
assertions.certainty_reason: A conceptual statement in a vendor page, without derivation.

assertions.value: The page defines the Q-factor as a measure of quality that determines how many round trips the light can make in a component before being lost.
quotes: One measure of this quality is the Q-factor, which determines how many round trips the light can make in a component before being lost
assertions.certainty_reason: The page's own definition of the Q-factor, Non-linear optics section.

assertions.value: The authors report that their hardware team demonstrated a Q-factor of the order of one hundred thousand in a cited paper, using manufacturing techniques very similar to those of the core technology.
assertions.anchor: Non-linear optics, citing the Optica 6(9) 1244 paper listed under Further reading
quotes: in this paper our hardware team was able to demonstrate a Q-factor of the order of one hundred thousand
using very similar manufacturing techniques to our core technology.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the page attributes to a separate paper by the company's own team; the page gives no measurement detail.
assertions.reader_inference: The page does not name the material or the device in this sentence; the linked paper would settle that.

assertions.value: The authors state that the company is developing a cutting-edge foundry to build the chips it needs, and that it hopes one day to make interactions strong enough that single particles of light bounce off each other.
quotes: For this reason we are developing a cutting-edge foundry to build the chips we need to do this.
We hope to one day make the interactions strong enough that even single particles of light can be made to "bounce" off each other.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's statement of its own plans and goals.
assertions.reader_inference: The word 'hope' implies that interactions this strong are not yet achieved on the company's devices as of this page.

assertions.value: The page states that quantum superposition allows a system to explore many possibilities in parallel but is only useful if coupled with quantum interference, which arises because quantum amplitudes can add or subtract while probabilities can only add.
quotes: Quantum superposition allows a system to effectively explore many possibilities in parallel, although it is only useful if we can also couple it with quantum interference.
unlike probabilities which can only add, quantum amplitudes can add or subtract
assertions.certainty_reason: A textbook-level statement given in a vendor page without derivation.

assertions.value: The page states that quantum interference is at the heart of the Grover speedup, where a quantum system can search for a solution much faster than any non-quantum method in a way that is rigorously provable, and that this can have practical implications such as solving hard optimization problems faster.
quotes: at the heart of the famed Grover speedup where a quantum system can search for a solution much faster than any non-quantum method in a way that is rigorously provable.
This kind of speedup can have practical implications, for example in solving hard optimization problems faster.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result attributed to prior work (Grover), stated without its conditions on this page.
assertions.reader_inference: The page gives no size of the speedup. Grover search is a quadratic speedup in query count, not an arbitrary one, and the page states no conditions; this is a loose summary.

assertions.value: The page states that quantum superpositions are fragile because interaction with the outside world destroys them, that photons can be relatively easily isolated from their environment, and that this together with the company's tools for manipulating photons gives a path toward large-scale quantum interference.
quotes: Quantum superpositions are fragile since they can be destroyed by interacting with the outside world
photons can be relatively easily isolated from their environment
gives us a path toward harnessing large-scale quantum interference.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its approach; no measurement is given.

assertions.value: The page states that the fragility of quantum superposition is a valuable asset for cybersecurity applications, because it makes it possible to tell if communications are being watched.
quotes: This fragility is a valuable asset for cybersecurity applications, as it makes it possible to tell if communications are being watched.
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement in a vendor page without supporting argument or reference.

assertions.value: The page uses a Galton board analogy to state that classically, moving a pipe from the winning to the losing cup can only decrease the chance of winning, while in the quantum version amplitudes can subtract, so the same move can increase the chance of winning and could even make losing impossible.
quotes: moving a pipe from the winning to the losing cup can only ever decrease your chance of winning. Probabilities can only add.
moving a pipe from the winning to the losing cup can increase your chances of winning, and could even make it impossible to lose.
assertions.certainty_reason: An analogy offered for teaching, not a derivation.

assertions.value: The page describes the Hong-Ou-Mandel effect: identical photons hitting either side of a 50% reflecting mirror leave in the same direction because the amplitudes for both reflecting and both transmitting subtract; it states the effect was first demonstrated in 1987 and is now routinely observed.
assertions.anchor: Some Examples, Hong Ou Mandel Effect
quotes: If identical particles of light hit either side of a special mirror which has a 50% chance of reflecting them and a 50% chance of them going straight through
the amplitudes subtract rather than add due to the physics of reflection, this effect is called the Hong-Ou-Mandel effect
it was first demonstrated in 1987 and now can be routinely observed in quantum optics labs around the world.
assertions.certainty_reason: A well-known result attributed to earlier experiments, described on this page without a citation.
assertions.reader_inference: The page's wording that the photons are always observed to leave in the same direction, 'meaning one reflects and one transmits', is garbled: in the standard effect both photons leave through the same output port, so the two outputs are never one each.

assertions.value: The page states that in the original Hong-Ou-Mandel experiment pairs could be measured a little more than once per second, and that the technology behind the company's devices can produce millions of high-quality photon pairs per second.
quotes: in that experiment, pairs could be measured a little more than once per second
can produce millions of high-quality photon pairs per second
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own technology; no measurement conditions are given.
assertions.reader_inference: The page gives no conditions for 'high-quality' and does not say whether the rate is from a device or a lab setup.

assertions.value: The page states that the Hong-Ou-Mandel effect can only be observed if single light particles can be reliably produced, and that a non-linear crystal was at the heart of the setup of the famous experiment in the 1980s.
quotes: This effect can only be observed if you can reliably produce single light particles
a non-linear crystal was at the heart of the setup of this famous experiment even in the 1980s.
assertions.certainty_reason: A historical statement given without a citation on this page.

assertions.value: The page states that the Hong-Ou-Mandel experiment was used to measure the size of the light particles, that waves of light only tens of micrometers long were produced, and that tens of thousands of them could fit in a single meter of fiber optics.
quotes: the purpose of the experiment was not actually to show quantum effects, but to use those effects to measure the size of the light particles
waves of light which were only tens of micrometers long, meaning that tens of thousands of them could fit in a single meter of fiber optics.
assertions.certainty_reason: A historical result stated without citation or measurement detail.

assertions.value: The page states that light is an ideal platform for processing large amounts of information because it can carry a lot of information and process it quickly, and that quantum effects take this potential further, making optics and photonics key technologies for computing and sensing.
quotes: Light is already an ideal platform for processing large amounts of information efficiently
making optics and photonics (the manipulation of light where the particle nature is important) key technologies for the processing of information for computing but also for sensing
assertions.certainty_reason: A promotional statement without evidence on the page.

assertions.value: The page states, as a limitation of lab-table quantum optics experiments with bolted-on components, that this approach is not scalable and cannot be practically integrated into devices, and that the company will therefore build its systems on chips.
quotes: While many famous quantum optics experiments have been performed on lab tables where components can be bolted on, this is not scalable and cannot be practically integrated into devices.
For this reason, we will build our systems on chips.
assertions.certainty_reason: The page states this limit and its consequence for the company's design in the Quantum optics on a chip section.

assertions.value: The authors state that the company is building a cutting-edge foundry to make quantum optical chips out of lithium niobate, a material already widely used in telecommunications devices, whose properties suit optical devices and waveguides.
quotes: We are building a cutting-edge foundry to build quantum optical chips out of lithium niobate, a material which is already widely used within telecommunications devices.
Lithium niobate has many ideal properties both for optical devices and for manufacturing waveguides
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own product and plans.

assertions.value: The authors state that ring resonators will be a workhorse of the devices, that they concentrate light using finely tuned microscopic rings, and that they can be tuned so that two light particles combine to make a light particle of another frequency, a process the page calls parametric conversion.
quotes: A workhorse of our devices will be ring resonators, these components allow light to be concentrated using finely tuned shaping of microscopic rings.

These resonators can be tuned so that two light particles (either the same or different frequencies) can combine to make a light particle of another frequency. This process is known as parametric conversion.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own device design.

assertions.value: The page states that a Zeno blockade is a quantum effect where a strong interaction can prevent a light particle from entering a cavity when another one is already there, because a particle needs time for its probability to build up in the cavity and a disruption such as a measurement or strong interaction can blockade it.
quotes: a Zeno blockade , where a strong interaction can actually prevent a light particle from entering a cavity when another one is already there.
if something disrupts this process, for example measurements or a strong interaction with a different particle then the particle can be blockaded.
assertions.certainty_reason: A conceptual description in a vendor page without derivation.

assertions.value: The authors state that a high enough quality ring resonator can make a single light particle bounce off another single light particle, using another light particle as the watcher in the Zeno blockade, and that such interactions would take non-linear optics to the ultimate quantum extreme.
quotes: In this way a high enough quality ring resonator can make a single light particle bounce off another single light particle.
Such interactions would allow us to take non-linear optics to the ultimate quantum extreme, making individual light particles interact.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of what its own devices can do; the cited Scientific Reports paper is listed under Further reading.
assertions.reader_inference: The sentence is conditional on a 'high enough quality' resonator; the page elsewhere says the company hopes to reach this strength one day, so it is not stated as achieved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that information can be encoded by sending light in different pulses, that more information can be added by allowing more space for the light to travel, and that this makes the devices highly scalable; they call it one of many encodings and a current focus.
quotes: we can encode large amounts of information by sending light in different pulses. More information can be added by just allowing more space for the light to travel.
Such designs make our devices highly scalable.
This is only one of many ways in which information can be encoded
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own design choice.

assertions.value: The authors state that non-linear optics converts weak laser pulses, or weak coherent states, into more interesting quantum states of light, so the chips can be powered by off-the-shelf lasers, and that these states can include squeezed states which use quantum effects to overcome some fundamental limits of classical optics.
quotes: Non-linear optics allow us to convert weak laser pulses, or "weak coherent states" into more interesting quantum states of light
our chips can be effectively powered by off-the-shelf lasers
These states can include "squeezed" states of light, which can use quantum effects to overcome some of the fundamental limitations of classical optics.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own product.

assertions.value: The page states that it is a high-level overview and points to the company's research for more depth; it keeps the explanation at a conceptual level and does not give the full mathematical explanation of why non-linear optics is needed.
quotes: This page is a high-level overview.

There is a full mathematical explanation for why this is true and why the non-linear optics which is at the core of our technology is needed, but here we will keep the explanation on more of a conceptual level.
assertions.certainty_reason: The page states its own scope in the opening paragraph and in Further reading.
assertions.reader_inference: Every statement on the page is therefore conceptual and uncited unless a link is given in Further reading.

assertions.value: The page lists, as its supporting work, a Physical Review Letters paper on producing single light particles that uses Hong-Ou-Mandel tests (DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.125.263602), a Scientific Reports paper on bouncing single photons off each other, an Optica paper on high-quality devices, an Optica conference abstract on ring resonators (CQO-2019-W5A.11), and a patent on strong non-linear quantum optical interactions (US11754908B2).
quotes: Some of the tests rely on the Hong-Ou-Mandel effect. https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.125.263602
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-017-13327-x
https://opg.optica.org/abstract.cfm?uri=CQO-2019-W5A.11
https://patents.google.com/patent/US11754908B2/en
assertions.certainty_reason: A list of links given by the page; the page does not report the results of these works.
assertions.reader_inference: These links are the primary sources for the page's device claims and could be read as their own records.
